data.name: Maratib
data.gender_notes: Maratib is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Islamic terminology, Maratib refers to various levels or degrees of spiritual attainment, as mentioned in the Quran and Hadith. The name signifies the journey towards Allah and the different stages of spiritual growth. The name Maratib carries the meaning “Levels, Degrees, Stages” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Maratib usually hope their child will grow to embody levels, degrees, stages and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A journey of faith and self-improvement
data.etymology: Maratib belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Levels, Degrees, Stages.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maratib total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_arabic.name: مَرَاتِب
in_arabic.meaning: مُشَكِّلَةُ مَرَاتِبُ الأُصُولِ فِي الأَنَامِ تَضُمُّ الْعُلومَ وَالأَخلاقَ
in_arabic.long_meaning: مَرَاتِبُ في الأَلَفِظِ الَّتِي تَخَلَّفُ عَنِ الأَصَلِ وَتُشَكِّلُ مَرَاتِبَ الأُصُولِ فِي الأَنَامِ، وَهِيَ مُشَكِّلَةُ مَخَزُونِ الأَخلاقِ وَالْعُلومِ، وَالَّتِي تَضُمُّ مَعَ الشُروعِ في حَيَاةِ الإِسْلَامِ، فَتُشَكِّلُ مَرَاتِبَ الأُصُولِ فِي الأَنَامِ، وَهِيَ مَشَرَقَةُ الأَخلاقِ وَالْعُلومِ

in_urdu.name: مراتب
in_urdu.meaning: مُشَكِّلَةُ مَرَاتِبُ الأُصُولِ فِي اَلانامِ تَضُمُّ اَلعُلومَ وَالاَخلاقَ
in_urdu.long_meaning: مراتب اَللفظ اَلتِی تَخلَفُ عَن اَلصل اَلتِی تُشَكِّلُ مراتِب اَلأُسُولِ فِي اَلانام، وَهِی مُشَكِّلَةُ مَخزون اَلاخلاقِ وَاَلعُلوم، اَلتِی تَضُمُّ مَعَ اَلشُرُوعِ فِي حَیاةٍ اِسلامیة، فَتُشَكِّلُ مراتِب اَلأُسُولِ فِي اَلانام، وَهِی مَشرقَة اَلاخلاقِ وَاَلعُلوم

in_english.name: Maratib
in_english.meaning: Levels of excellence, ranks of virtues, and degrees of knowledge
in_english.long_meaning: Maratib refers to the levels of excellence, ranks of virtues, and degrees of knowledge in human beings. It encompasses the philosophers and virtuous individuals who embody the principles of Islam. The concept of Maratib highlights the importance of moral character and intellectual pursuits in human development, emphasizing the need for individuals to strive for excellence in both their spiritual and intellectual lives.

data.cultural_impact: The name Maratib holds a rich cultural significance in the Islamic world, as it relates to the concept of Sufism, which is an integral part of Islamic spirituality. The idea of progressing through different stations or levels of spiritual development is a central theme in Sufi teachings and practices. Thus, the name Maratib is often associated with Sufism and the spiritual journey towards Allah.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Maratib represents the progressive stages of one's journey towards Allah. It is a reminder that the path towards spiritual growth is not a linear one, but rather a dynamic and unfolding process. Each stage of this journey brings with it new insights, challenges, and opportunities for growth. The name Maratib serves as a reminder that we should strive to deepen our spiritual connections with Allah and continuously seek to expand our knowledge and understanding of the divine. Ultimately, it is a call to focus on the inner journey towards elevating the soul, rather than simply indulging in external material pursuits.

historical_references.context: Maratib is mentioned as a fortress belonging to the Hafsid rulers of Ifriqiya, located near the city of Tunis. It was known for its strategic importance in controlling trade routes and defend against invaders.

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi's The Histories of the Prophets and Kings: The Sultanate of Egypt under the Burjis (1352-1382 CE)
historical_references.context: Maratib is mentioned as the name of a fortress or palace located in Cairo. It was a residence of the Burjis, who were a non-Arab Turkic ruling dynasty, and was known for its grandeur and magnificence.
